fields.value: Fail one match, not the whole evaluation, when a game process hangs or dies

Problem. The evaluation game pool (src/etude/eval/run.py, at d9a6bc8) has no per-match isolation:
- Hang: there is no per-match time bound, only the run's ETUDE_DEADLINE. A game stuck inside a native call holds its worker until the deadline; then "evaluation deadline reached before a match completed" raises RetryRequested and every pending match of every grouped evaluation fails with retry.
- Process death (abort, segfault, out-of-memory kill): the future raises BrokenProcessPool, which becomes RetryRequested("game process exited before returning its match") for the whole group. A match that deterministically kills its process does this on every pass, so the group never completes.

Outcome.
- An author can declare a per-match time bound on an evaluation job.
- A game process that dies or exceeds that bound fails that one match as an ordinary game failure (retained, replayed only with --retry-failed), named with the reason. The pool replaces the worker and unrelated matches, in this and other grouped evaluations, continue.
- The run deadline, agent-process failure and infrastructure retry keep their present behavior.

Constraints and notes.
- ProcessPoolExecutor cannot kill or replace a single worker (the code already reaches into pool._processes to reap on cancellation), so this likely means Etude managing its spawned game processes itself; keep initialize_game, the import report and Performance records per match.
- A killed game holding an agent connection must not strand a batch: the agent process already tolerates a closed peer.
- Document the bound and the failure in docs/evaluation.md and docs/limits.md.

Why now. Manabot (MTG-329) is adopting Agents(load, build) and moving its games into Etude's game processes. Until now it ran each group of games in its own bounded subprocess, so a hang or hard crash cost one group; in-process, it costs the whole grouped evaluation. Manabot handles catchable Rust panics and cooperative game time limits itself; this Task covers what only the process owner can: true hangs and hard exits.
